notes: The 1969 volume of the Recreation and Park Commission. Curated: design approvals, the Palace of Fine Arts theater agreement, landmark recognition in Golden Gate Park.

coverage.remaining: Routine items not curated; the Candlestick Park enlargement (John Bolles) not curated. Not placed: the debate over remodeling the old Police Academy at 37th Avenue and Fulton for senior citizens (Aug 7; outcome not legible), the Portsmouth Square play area to be added under the bridge (Sep 25), the Huntington Park Christmas tree plaque (Mar 13).
coverage.note: Index runs to about line 26,000; few meeting openers survive, so dated by footers (Oct 17 was an 8:15 a.m. special meeting). Curated list F1969.py.

findings.address_as_written: Helen Crocker Russell Library, Strybing Arboretum
findings.description: The Recreation and Park Commission approved the final plans by Yuill-Thornton, Warner & Levikow for the Helen Crocker Russell Library, an addition to the arboretum's existing building paid for by private subscription through the Strybing Arboretum Society, which was to build it and deed it to the city.

citation.label: Minutes of the Recreation and Park Commission, August 7, 1969

findings.address_as_written: Golden Gate Park - Designation of Conservatory as Landmark
findings.description: The Landmarks Preservation Advisory Board proposed to the Recreation and Park Commission that the Conservatory be the first of Golden Gate Park's buildings designated a city landmark, following a suggestion to the park's centennial committee; the Commission's president questioned handing responsibility for its preservation to another agency and suggested providing for it in the park's master plan instead.

citation.label: Minutes of the Recreation and Park Commission, September 11, 1969

findings.description: The Recreation and Park Commission approved an agreement with Vincent G. Raney, architect, for preliminary plans of a little theater of about 1,000 seats in the Palace of Fine Arts, estimated at $562,000, on condition that no further fee be paid if the plans were not approved or money for building it was not found.
